To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified five genes within the MEN1 region and have characterized their expression in several endocrine tumour types.
the MEN1 gene is located on chromosome 11q13 and encodes a protein that has a role in calcium‐dependent signalling pathways.
we have cloned five genes from a 900 kb region containing the MEN1 locus on human chromosome 11.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of the MEN1 gene by the positional cloning approach, and the characterization of the gene products.
the molecular characterization of the five candidates and the search for mutations in the coding regions of these genes.
the identification of the MEN1 gene by the analysis of cDNA candidates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gene responsible for the development of the MEN1 tumours has not been found.
MEN1 is a complex genetic disease with a number of different mutations in different genes.
the phospholipase gene is the best candidate for the MEN1 locus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MEN1 may be located within the interval between D7S522 and D7S504.
we have identified a number of candidate genes for MEN1, including the phospholipase‐Cβ3 gene, and that the latter gene is a strong candidate for MEN1.
we have isolated five cDNAs, three of them are expressed in normal tissues and two in tumours.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MEN1 locus contains several candidate tumour‐suppression genes.
MEN1 is not a single gene.
the MEN1 locus is likely to contain a single gene, and that phospholipase‐C‐β3 is a good candidate to be the gene responsible for MEN1.
